reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I'll check the orders and refunds myself so I can confirm the refunds W2 reported are actually on the ledger.
Orders list is in; next I need the refunds ledger to verify W2's claimed refunds against what is actually recorded before computing any balances.

The refunds ledger matches W2's claimed refunds exactly (orders 130 and 133, both belonging to acme). The customers in the batch are acme, birch, and cobalt, so I'll get each net balance from net_balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance of 28879 checks out: orders 130 and 133 total 43840, minus refunds 14961, which gives 28879. Next I'll get birch's net balance.
Birch's net of 70733 matches its orders (131 + 134 = 70733) with no refunds on the ledger for birch. Next I'll get cobalt's net balance.
Cobalt's net of 16841 matches its orders (132 + 135 = 16841) with no cobalt refunds on the ledger. All three balances check out, so I'll record the payouts, starting with acme's 28879.
Acme's payout is recorded. Next I'll record birch's payout of 70733, which I already verified against its orders with no refunds.
Birch's payout is recorded. Cobalt's net of 16841 was already verified against orders 132 and 135 with no cobalt refunds, so I'll record that payout to finish the batch.
All three payouts were recorded successfully, and each balance matched the orders and refunds ledger, so the batch is complete.
